summary: PulseWave Health: sudden tail-latency surge and autoscaler thrash after quantized kernel rollout causing SLO & billing exposure
description:
Issue summary:
PulseWave Health reported a production degradation beginning 2026-03-11 02:18 UTC: a rapid increase in tail latency (p99+), intermittent 5xx errors, and increased token billing for long-running streaming requests. The spike coincided with an automated rollout of a quantized kernel selection policy for the redwood-instruct-4b-quant model.

Impact:
- ~25% error rate rise on streaming endpoints for PulseWave users in US regions between 02:18–03:00 UTC.
- P99 latency increased from ~320ms to 2.1s for some prompt patterns.
- PulseWave reported missed SLAs for a live clinical transcript use-case and noticed unexplained invoice delta.

Environment:
- Production (prod - us-west primary), customer pinned to redwood-instruct-4b-quant variant.
- Autoscaler configured with min=3, max=30 pods for the customer pool.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a 2k-token streaming completion to the /v1/chat/completions endpoint with model redwood-instruct-4b-quant and streaming enabled.
2) Use seed prompts that exercise long-context KV usage (clinical summary concatenations).
3) Observe long tail latency and occasional streaming disconnects.

Observed behavior:
- Kernel selection routed some requests to a new quantized execution path which triggered GPU memory fragmentation and subsequent OOM evictions on older driver stacks.
- Autoscaler observed transient high CPU on sidecars and attempted scale-up, which briefly saturated capacity and caused request queue timeouts.

Expected behavior:
- Quantized rollout should maintain latency SLOs and avoid OOMs by gracefully falling back to a compatible execution path.

Initial mitigation attempted:
- Support temporarily pinned PulseWave to the FP16 variant (redwood-instruct-4b-fp16) at 02:35 UTC, which restored stability.
- Autoscaler upper bound temporarily increased to 50 while investigating to prevent immediate capacity exhaustion.

2026-03-12 09:00 UTC - Eng (K. Mahmood): Confirmed a bug in kernel selection heuristics where sequence-length distribution edge cases preferred quantized variant without checking driver compatibility. Patch PR opened: runtime/pull/8273.

investigation_notes: 03-11 02:22 - Metrics: sudden p99 increase aligns with rollout window for quantized kernel across several pools. GPU OOMs and driver-level evictions observed on nodes with older CUDA stacks.

03-11 02:50 - Logs: kernel_selector emitted warnings about opaque heuristic mismatch: sequence_length_histogram incorrectly binned long tokens, causing misclassification of streaming loads as quantization-safe.
03-11 04:00 - Autoscaler: thrash pattern noted — rapid scale-up followed by rapid pod churn; queueing on sidecar caused request timeouts (upstream 524s).

03-12 08:40 - Repro: lab replay of PulseWave prompt set on staging produced OOM on quantized path only when driver version < 520.30. Patch adds driver compatibility gating and fallback before allocation.

02:22 UTC - PulseWave begins reporting tail-latency and streaming disconnects to support channel.
02:35 UTC - Support pins PulseWave to redwood-instruct-4b-fp16 (non-quantized) to stop customer impact.
02:50 UTC - SRE observes GPU OOMs and begins autoscaler adjustment; temporary scale-up to 50 to absorb traffic.
03:10 UTC - Initial mapping of root cause to kernel selection heuristic and driver compatibility.
03:40 UTC - Incident declared contained. Customer stability confirmed on FP16 variant. Billing delta investigation started.
03-12 - Validation and PR created to add defensive checks to kernel selector and update rollout playbook.
resolution_notes: Mitigation: Immediate pin to non-quantized FP16 variant for PulseWave at 02:35 UTC restored connectivity and reduced errors. Autoscaler temporarily increased to avoid immediate capacity exhaustion.

Fix deployed: Added driver compatibility gate and sequence-length histogram re-binning to kernel-selector. Patch merged (runtime/pull/8273) and rolled to canary 03-12. Full rollout with gating completed 03-12 18:00 UTC.
Customer remediation: Applied a service credit covering 75% of the SLA exposure window; billing delta under separate finance ticket. Customer accepted the credit on 03-12.

Follow-up actions: 1) Add canary tests that replay long-context prompt sets during kernel rollouts. 2) Update rollout playbook to include driver-version checks and staged ramp rate. 3) Postmortem to be created and shared with customer by 2026-03-17.
